improvement_notes: Clarify explicitly that the robot reference point is the midpoint of the drive-wheel axle/contact pair, since the equations for v and omega depend on that choice.

Define the positive heading convention relative to the initial pose earlier in the lesson, then connect the visual ‘upward’ orientation and the Python ‘positive x’ orientation more explicitly. The current transition is technically recoverable but may momentarily confuse beginners.

Replace or supplement the generic alt text for diagram.png with a content-specific description of the schematic’s blocks, signals, and relationships. The current instruction to ‘trace the signal’ presumes that the diagram visibly contains such a signal flow.

The challenge asks students to replace a case in the code but does not ask them to inspect heading numerically. Add a small heading-output task so the spin case and curved-motion case are represented in both position and orientation.

Add one short warning that commanded wheel speeds, measured wheel speeds, and motor power are different quantities. This distinction is mentioned later, but introducing it before the Python lab would better prevent a common implementation mistake.

The section sequence is strong but slightly long for a foundational kinematics lesson. The repeated explanations of straight motion, equal speeds, and the faster-right-wheel case could be compressed to preserve attention for the lab and real-robot limitations.

For accessibility, ensure equations are accompanied by plain-language interpretations in the rendered course platform and that color is not the sole way the generated diagrams distinguish left turns, right turns, or wheel roles.
